schema.label: Volumes and constraints
schema.text: CTV is chest wall (and expander, implant, or autologous mound when reconstructed), axilla levels 1 to 3, supraclavicular nodes, and internal mammary nodes. Chest wall CTV stops at the anterior ribs and intercostal muscles unless those structures are involved, and it excludes the first 3 mm under the skin. Internal mammary CTV is a 4 to 5 mm expansion on the vessels from the fourth rib to the caudal supraclavicular volume. Two or three anterior fields are angled 45 to 60 degrees apart. Coverage goal is CTV D95 at least 95 percent and D0.01 cm3 at most 110 percent. Ipsilateral lung V40 percent of prescription is at most 15 percent, mean heart dose is at most 1.5 percent of prescription, brachial plexus D0.01 cm3 is at most 102 percent, and esophagus D1 cm3 is at most 72 percent. Skin objectives are also specified. A nodal boost is allowed for undissected, clinically involved internal mammary, infraclavicular, or supraclavicular nodes. A chest wall boost is not allowed.

schema.text: Pembrolizumab 200 mg intravenously every 3 weeks until progression, death, or unacceptable toxicity. No dose reductions. Interruptions up to 12 weeks are allowed. eligibility: Age 18 or older. ECOG 2 or lower. Histologically confirmed metastatic solid tumor with at least one brain metastasis measuring at least 5 mm. Dexamethasone must be stable at 2 mg or less for at least 7 days.

publications.title: Salvage chemoradiation therapy for recurrence after radical surgery or palliative surgery in esophageal cancer patients: a prospective, multicenter clinical trial protocol.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: One-arm multicenter prospective trial of modular salvage chemoradiation for thoracic esophageal squamous cell carcinoma after esophagectomy. Patients are assigned, not randomized, to elective nodal irradiation or involved-field irradiation.

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: R1 or R2 resection, locoregional recurrence after radical surgery, out-of-field recurrence after adjuvant radiotherapy, or recurrence after adjuvant chemotherapy. Age 16-70 years, KPS at least 70, no distant metastasis, and no prior therapy for the recurrence.

schema.label: Stratify
schema.text: Assignment uses, in steps, R0 versus R1/R2 surgery, recurrent-lesion diameter, involved regions, and time to recurrence. Dose and technique are then modified by distance from the lesion to the thoracic stomach or intestine.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Two volume strategies, both with concurrent chemotherapy: paclitaxel 135-150 mg/m2 on day 1 plus lobaplatin or nedaplatin every 3 weeks for two cycles. Optional consolidation uses the same regimen.

arms.label: Elective nodal irradiation
arms.text: Prophylactic high-risk nodal CTV. For a lesion far from the thoracic stomach, the published SIB-IMRT example is PTV 50.4 Gy in 28 fractions and PGTV 59.92-62.16 Gy in 28 fractions. SIB versus sequential boost is chosen for stomach or bowel safety. If thoracic-stomach V50 exceeds 50%, the total dose is reduced to 45 Gy in 25 fractions.

arms.label: Involved-field irradiation
arms.text: CTV is GTV plus 0.6-0.8 cm radially and 1.0-1.5 cm craniocaudally, with no elective nodes. Away from stomach: 60 Gy in 30 fractions. Close to stomach: 59.4-61.2 Gy in 33-34 fractions. The same V50 stomach reduction to 45 Gy in 25 fractions applies.

schema.note: Not a randomized comparison. The exact decision tree is in the protocol figure.

brief.schema_source: The open-access protocol states stepwise assignment to elective nodal or involved-field salvage chemoradiation and gives the dose schedules.
eligibility: R1 or R2 resection, locoregional recurrence after radical surgery, out-of-field recurrence after adjuvant chemoradiation or radiotherapy, or recurrence after adjuvant chemotherapy. No therapy yet for the recurrence. Age 16 to 70. Karnofsky performance status at least 70.
Normal blood count, with white cells above 4.0 x 10^9/L specified. Liver and kidney function are called satisfactory, without numeric cutoffs in the text read.

Excluded: another malignancy within 5 years, pregnancy or lactation, drug allergy, refusal of consent, non-regional nodes other than supraclavicular or celiac, distant metastasis, and severe cardiovascular disease, infection, active ulcer, unstable diabetes, or mental disorder.

registry_schema.label: Design
registry_schema.text: This research study is being done to study if less intensive treatments can be used after surgery for head and neck cancers that are due to the human papilloma virus (HPV). In general, these cancers have better cure rates than other types of head and neck cancers. Therefore, the investigators are studying whether we can safely reduce the amount of treatment after surgery, such as surveillance (instead of using radiation) or less radiation or less chemotherapy, while maintaining good cure rates. The investigators hope that by reducing the intensity of treatment, this will lead to less side effects during and after cancer treatment.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: POTENTIAL is a prospective multicenter open-label phase 3 trial of internal mammary node irradiation after mastectomy in high-risk axillary node-positive breast cancer. Planned enrollment is 1800. Patients are required to receive at least six cycles of anthracycline and/or taxane-based chemotherapy.

schema.label: Stratify
schema.text: Randomization is stratified by institution, tumor location (medial or central versus other quadrants), number of positive axillary nodes (1-3 versus 4-9 versus at least 10), and neoadjuvant chemotherapy (yes versus no).

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Patients are randomly assigned 1:1 to postmastectomy radiotherapy with or without internal mammary node irradiation. CT-based 3D conformal radiotherapy, intensity-modulated radiotherapy, or volumetric modulated arc therapy may be used. Prescribed dose is 50 Gy in 25 fractions or 43.5 Gy in 15 fractions.

arms.label: No IMNI

eligibility: Women age 18 to 70 with histologically confirmed invasive breast cancer, ECOG 0 to 2, able to tolerate radiotherapy, and willing to be followed.

Total mastectomy and axillary dissection of at least 10 nodes with negative margins. No one-stage reconstruction. Sentinel biopsy alone, or internal mammary dissection or sentinel biopsy, is excluded.

Node risk: at least 4 positive axillary nodes; or 1 to 3 positive nodes and T3 to 4; or 1 to 3 positive nodes and T1 to 2 with a high-risk score of at least 3 (age 40 or younger, inner quadrant, 2 to 3 positive nodes, lymphovascular invasion, and stage points as specified); or ypN+ after neoadjuvant chemotherapy.

No imaging evidence of supraclavicular or internal mammary metastases before and after systemic therapy, and no distant metastases. Internal mammary nodes must have been imaged before systemic therapy.
At least six cycles of anthracycline and/or taxane chemotherapy. Endocrine therapy for 5 years and anti-HER2 therapy for 1 year are anticipated when indicated. LVEF at least 50 percent.

Excluded: bilateral breast cancer, severe cardiac insufficiency, myocardial infarction or uncorrected unstable arrhythmia or unstable angina in the last 3 months, pericardial disease, prior chest wall or supraclavicular radiotherapy, and another malignancy except non-melanoma skin cancer, papillary or follicular thyroid carcinoma, cervical carcinoma in situ, or contralateral noninvasive breast cancer.

schema.text: Noncontrolled, single-arm phase 2 protocol for patients older than 18 years with high-grade soft tissue sarcomas of the girdles or extremities. Three neoadjuvant cycles of ifosfamide and doxorubicin are given. Hypofractionated radiotherapy, 25 Gy in 5 fractions over 5 days, is given in the second cycle, and that cycle is doxorubicin only. After surgery, patients whose specimen contains less than 30% viable cells receive three additional full chemotherapy cycles.

eligibility: Age 18 to 75. Nonmetastatic high-grade soft tissue sarcoma of an extremity, or the pelvic or shoulder girdle, confirmed by pathology.
Primary or recurrent tumor that cannot be resected with a 1.0 to 2.0 cm three-dimensional margin, or for which limb preservation is not possible. No prior chemotherapy or radiotherapy.

Karnofsky index above 70 percent. Leukocytes above 3500/mm3, neutrophils above 1500/mm3, platelets above 100,000/mm3, creatinine below 1.5 mg/dL, bilirubin within normal limits, transaminases at most twice normal, and no coronary disease by ejection fraction.
Excluded: embryonal rhabdomyosarcoma, primitive neuroectodermal tumor, chondrosarcoma, osteosarcoma, HIV, pelvic or thoracic organs in the radiation field, and refusal of consent.

pretreatment.note: CT or ultrasound for extremity liposarcoma.
Used to exclude coronary artery disease.

specimens.note: One pathologist grades the tumor. A slice from the least necrotic area is mapped in 1.0 to 2.0 cm2 cuts. Mean percent viable cells determines whether adjuvant chemotherapy is offered. The threshold is 30 percent or less.

registry_schema.text: A proton beam is made up of charged particles that have a well-defined range of penetration into tissues. How deep it can penetrate is decided by both the beam's energy and the density of the tissue through which it passes. As the proton beam penetrates the body, the particles slow down, and the beam deposits its dose sharply near the end of its range. This is a phenomenon known as the Bragg peak. By adjusting the Bragg peak, the doctor can deliver a full, localized, uniform dose of energy to the treatment site while sparing the surrounding normal tissues.
